convoLines.text: "This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Get to their side of the Haven door and stand next to them — then you can help.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"This one — Water Chestnut. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Mahua — crush the leaf, smell it, taste the stem. That's how you know it."
"Have you heard what they're calling The Algorithm? Lillian is pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hear me out — Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
Hannah has an edge today — something curdled.
"This one — Cassava. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Tucumã — crush the leaf, smell it, taste the stem. That's how you know it."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I — I don't remember saying that." A beat. "People hear what they want to hear."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"Huh. Let me think about that." Everyone gets forgotten eventually. I'm negotiating for later rather than sooner.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Someday someone will tell my story wrong. I just hope they tell it funny."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Buse grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Hannah is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I don't know what to do with my hands today."
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"We lost Buse and Hannah. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"I save the best bite for last. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"The fire feels smaller without Hannah. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here? You'd know about that."
"Can I be honest? The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"Practical view: butchery. Sounds small. But small useful things stack — and one day you look up and you're the person everyone asks. That's how it happens."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Zinhle looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hey — Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Bottom line: Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"I count meals, not days. Three meals since the rain. Two since the alarm. Days are for people with calendars. I have a stomach. How are you holding up, though?"
"Still on what day it is."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Hannah is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sit apart to eat at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about grief — we wandered off it, 7 days back. 'I — yeah. It helps, hearing that.' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
You walk to the trap line with Lillian. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Hannah died... I keep expecting to see Hannah at the fire. Stupid."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Sure — what's on your mind? ...sorry, lost it."

"Still on how this changed you."

"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "Hannah always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"Nobody says Hannah's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you don't recognize the person in your head anymore. Still a stranger to yourself?"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with Zinhle. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Rafael died... I keep expecting to see Rafael at the fire. Stupid."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind the creek water run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be remembered. The truth felt small. The lie felt like someone worth keeping around."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Serviceberry — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now. That means something."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
On the way, Zinhle stops and actually teaches you something — how they read a slope for water, how their grandmother did it. (Knowledge, freely given. The Codex notes it.)
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson. Worth considering."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"We're down to 6 liters of clean water. I can't carry enough alone. First light, the creek, you and me?"
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 6 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
"All right — let's ask them." You carry the proposal to The Bloodied II.

"We went over this," Priya says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."

Their whole posture softens around you.
"As I said — we're still on that personal stuff."

d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Leroy is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Thornfield watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Leroy Romano is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Leroy kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Leroy's gone." Ryan looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Leroy." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Shannon blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"

d41: The fire knew Shannon before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
